newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Rivals cry foul as Donetsk leads World Cities Chess.
newsitem.headline: Rivals cry foul as Donetsk leads World Cities Chess.

text.p: Donetsk retained the lead after the seventh round of the World Cities Chess Championship in Jakarta on Friday but in circumstances which had the Ukrainians' rivals crying foul.
Donetsk drew their match against Tashkent 2-2, the entire contest taking only 18 minutes.
Two games between the Ukrainians and the Uzbeks were agreed drawn after only 8 minutes, the remaining games took just 10 minutes longer.
"It's disgraceful - of course it was fixed," exclaimed an angry Einar Gausel, a member of the Oslo team which had been hot on Donetsk's heels.
"The match was disloyal to the spectators and the organisers," the Norwegian Grandmaster continued.
"In a 1992 team tournament it was discussed that both teams should be forfeited after such a match but I think nothing was done.
"The Jakarta organisers indicated that no action would be taken against the two teams since nothing could be proven.
"Typical Soviets," was one organiser's comment, a reference to the common practice of prearranging draws in the era of the USSR.
Another recalled that a similar match had been played between Russia and the Ukraine at the 1996 Chess Olympics, a result which helped give the silver medals to the Ukrainians.
With Oslo losing narrowly to Moscow, Donetsk's 2-2 result increased their lead to a point and they will be paired against an outgunned Rangoon team in the eighth round.
The Ukrainians are now hot favourites to become the first World Cities Champion and win the US$10,000 first prize.
Donetsk's match overshadowed what was otherwise an exceptionally hard-fought round which saw Bandung's fine run come to an end at the hands of fellow Indonesians Depok Margonda.
Ho Chi Minh City also kept their medal hopes alive with a narrow win over the surprising Filipino line-up from Mandaluyung.
The eighth round will be played on Sunday.
The World Cities Championship concludes on Monday.
